account:
Today has mostly involved ordinary appointments, accounts, and people offering their services, but there are a few unexplained reports. At tea, neighbour told me people were curious about bakery lights. Baker now says he has installed no new lights and arranged no special occasion. Builder reportedly said he had not installed them either. I have not inspected those lights myself, so I do not yet know whether anything actually changed or who might be responsible.

Neighbour traces a vague story about a crossing change to Townsfolk 02 and 22, neither of whom supplied details or evidence. Freight reportedly knew of no change. Builder directly reported that the bridge was passable, lanterns were present, and no defects or repairs were confirmed. There is therefore no verified crossing problem. I have asked neighbour to direct anyone with firsthand details to me tomorrow rather than spread speculation.

Builder sought a two-emerald inspection fee after the inspection, without an advance agreement. I declined it. He also offered the baker repairs or lighting, which the baker declined because he knew of no problem. These offers could simply be attempts to find paid work; I have no evidence of another purpose.

I saw freight hand secretary a written book. Secretary says it offers local delivery services for two emeralds per load, with cargo, route, and deadline agreed beforehand. She filed it with accounts and says no municipal work was authorized. Neighbour also saw baker give freight bread after a discussion of a market delivery. That seems compatible with ordinary trading or delivery business, though I do not know their actual agreement. Baker has been offering bread and asking whether town gatherings need supplies; I know of no scheduled gathering.

My present view is that several people are seeking business while an unsupported crossing rumor and unexplained talk about bakery lighting circulate. I cannot responsibly conclude there is a coordinated secret undertaking. The useful next steps are firsthand accounts from the rumor's sources and, if necessary, a direct look at the bakery lighting. My next scheduled obligation is home at seven, and tomorrow morning I should consult my appointment book again.
